To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

electrospray ionizaion with Fourier-transform mass specrtometry can be applied to verify the molecular weights of DNA and RNA sequences up to 100-nt long, and to identify and characterize impurities and adduction.
high-resolution electrospray mass spectrometry is a powerful technique for verifying the molecular weights of nucleotide sequences and for detecting impurities in oligomers.
high-resolution mass spectrometer measurements can verify the identity of single-stranded RNA and DNA molecules up to 100 nucleotides long.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mass spectrometric methods for the verification and characterization of DNA, RNA, and other biopolymers.
developing and implementing new methods in analytical chemistry and mass spectrometry to address problems of interest to the biological sciences.
developing new methods for the characterization of synthetic and natural oligonucleotide sequences.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mass of a 100-base single-stranded DNA is determined with an accuracy of 1 Da, and that of a tRNA with an accuracy of < 0.1 Da.
the molecular weight of the 100-mer is 30,702 +/- 2 Da.
the molecular mass of the sample has been measured with a precision of < 50 ppm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
high-resolution electrospray ionizaton with Fourier-transform mass analysis is an excellent technique for the verification of nucleic acid sequences.
high-resolution mass spectrometer can provide accurate verification of nucleotide sequences of 100-mer length.
the mass of a 100-molecule sample is determined with a 0.03% accuracy and 1- to 2-ppm reproducibility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
mass spectrometry is a valuable tool to verify DNA and RNA sequences.
mass spectrometry is a powerful technique to characterize nucleic acid sequences.
high-resolution mass spectometry can be a valuable tool for the analysis and verification of nucleic acid structures.
